chunks: I said to him: 'Sometimes I shoot with the blunt arrow (mi'rad) and I kill.' So he said: 'When it cuts it into two parts, throw away the smaller of the two and eat the larger. And if they are equal, then eat them both.'

key_terms.اعْتَدَلَا: They are equal — referring to the two pieces being of the same or comparable size.
key_terms.جَدْلَيْنِ: Two parts — the two halves or sections into which the prey is divided by the arrow's impact.
key_terms.مِعْرَاض: Mi'rad — a type of arrow with a blunt or transverse head, which kills by the force of impact rather than piercing. Hunting with it is permissible if it causes death by impact.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating prey hunted with a blunt arrow (mi'rad) that splits into two parts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding hunting with the mi'rad — a type of blunt or flat-headed arrow that kills by impact rather than penetration. The Imam rules that if such an arrow cuts the hunted prey into two unequal pieces, only the larger piece is permissible to eat (as it contains the vital organs and is the main body), while the smaller part is discarded. If the two parts are equal in size, both may be eaten. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that when an animal is slaughtered or killed in a manner that may be questionable, the portion containing the head and vital organs is the one whose lawfulness is confirmed.
